Problem 840. Reading an archaeological sequence: case 5
Archaeological layers provide relative chronological information. Dates from objects add constraints but do not automatically make every date exact.

An undisturbed archaeological site has four layers from top to bottom: A, B, C, D. In an undisturbed sequence, lower layers were deposited earlier. D contains an object dated 1320, C contains one dated 1510, and B contains one dated 1680. Cross-domain check: on a field sketch, 1 cm represents 2 km and two checkpoints are 2 cm apart.

In an undisturbed sequence, a lower layer is older than a layer above it. A securely dated object provides a constraint on the layer that contains it, but one object does not date every other object exactly. For the cross-domain check, real distance = sketch distance × kilometres per centimetre.
Which is older, Layer C or Layer B? Can the exact year of deposition of Layer A be deduced? Cross-domain check: what real distance separates the checkpoints?

1. C lies below B, so C is older than B by the stratigraphic rule. 2. No exact dated object or deposition year is given for A. 3. Therefore only relative ordering, not an exact year for A, is justified. Cross-domain check: 2×2=4 km.
Layer C is older than Layer B. The exact deposition year of Layer A cannot be deduced. Cross-domain answer: 4 km.

Problem 841. Applying a rule with an exception: Maya
Rules often have conditions and exceptions. Logical reading prevents us from applying a general rule when an overriding exception is active.

Maya is 13 years old. A library rule says: a child may enter the archive room if age ≥ 14 AND an adult permit is present. Exception: during an evacuation drill, nobody may enter. Permit present: yes. Evacuation drill: no.
Check exceptions first if they override the general rule. Otherwise every condition joined by AND must be true.
May Maya enter the archive room under these facts? Show which conditions succeed or fail.
1. Age test: 13≥14 is False. 2. Permit test is True. 3. Because the general rule uses AND, both tests must pass. 4. Therefore entry is not allowed.
The order of reasoning matters when exceptions override ordinary rules.
Boolean rule with priority: exception predicate first, then conjunction of eligibility conditions.
